summary: Round downward to the greatest integer no larger than a value.
documentation: Math.floor returns an integer-valued number by rounding toward negative infinity. Dividing a position by a positive bucket width and flooring the quotient assigns positions on both sides of zero to equal-width intervals.
inputs: An object with finite numeric position and a positive finite width; quotients have small magnitudes.
returns: The integer index of the half-open bucket containing the position.
caution: Negative fractions round to a more negative integer, unlike truncation. Binary floating-point division may approximate decimal boundaries; the supplied values avoid ambiguous boundaries.
scenarios: Assign a point to a tile in a coordinate grid that extends left of zero.
Group signed timeline offsets into fixed-width time buckets.
Compute a histogram bin from a measurement and its bin width.
title: Find the bucket across zero
problem: Return Math.floor(position / width). Bucket k covers positions from k * width inclusive to (k + 1) * width exclusive. Support negative positions.
hint: Floor the quotient, including when it lies between -1 and 0.
goal: Use Math.floor() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
